prompt:
Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Every category has a bidirectional nature. For example:

One person's sensitivity to the Care/Harm foundation may lead them to support high levels of immigration from poorer nations, to reduce the suffering of those who migrate. Whereas another person's sensitivity to the very same foundation may lead them to oppose those levels, because they believe it could lead to people they care about being harmed.

TEXT_D:
Scope
- Applies mainly to England due to devolution. Scottish and Welsh proposals may differ.

Fiscal approach and tax
- Reprioritise about £5bn annually by abolishing certain subsidies and departments/functions, cancelling ID cards, and diverting Child Trust Fund money to education.
- Introduce a 50% income tax rate only on earnings above £100,000 to fund: abolition of university tuition/top-up fees; free personal care for elderly/disabled people; and cutting local taxes by replacing Council Tax with a Local Income Tax based on ability to pay.
- Independent scrutiny of budgets by the National Audit Office; greater ONS independence.
- Typical household local tax bill reduced by about £450 under Local Income Tax.

Health and care
- Free personal care for elderly and disabled people.
- Faster diagnosis via expanded access to scans/tests, weekend/evening operation, and staffing/training.
- Free eye and dental checks; broaden prescription charge exemptions for long‑term conditions.
- More clinicians; scrap central targets; more local accountability.
- NHS dentistry contract reform and personal dental plans.
- Health MOTs, personal care plans for long‑term conditions, stronger mental health rights, end age discrimination.
- Public health: school nutrition standards, limit junk‑food ads to children, ban smoking in enclosed public places.

Education and skills
- Abolish tuition/top‑up fees; restore grants.
- Use Child Trust Fund budget to hire 21,000 teachers; infant classes average 20, junior 25; extended school hours; 3,500 Children’s Centres.
- Subject-specialist teaching in core subjects; reduce high‑stakes testing at 7 and 11; stronger SEN support; behaviour plans and managed transfers.
- Unified academic/vocational diplomas from 14; fund parity for colleges; maintain statutory school transport distances.
- Green building standards for education estates; strengthen outdoor learning.

Crime, justice, borders and equality
- 10,000 more police (funded by scrapping ID cards) plus complete 20,000 CSOs; cut police bureaucracy, modernise tech.
- Prioritise serious drug crime; expand tough community sentences; anti‑social behaviour tools with underlying support.
- Prisons focused on work, literacy and skills; progress tied to effort.
- Create a UK Border Force; protect jury trial; tighten judicial control of any control orders; allow intercept evidence; repeal flawed terror provisions.
- Overhaul asylum processing via a dedicated agency; allow asylum seekers to work; pursue EU common standards.
- Single Equality Act; hate‑crime units in every force.

Economy and business
- Stamp Duty threshold to £150,000.
- Simpler, lighter regulation with impact tests, sunset clauses, single inspections.
- Small‑business rate relief and site‑value rating; fair‑trading duty; English Tourism Board.
- Carbon Tax replacing the Climate Change Levy; incentives for cleaner vehicles and energy‑efficient homes.
- At least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; no replacement of aging nuclear plants.

Pensions, benefits and family support
- From 75: basic state pension to at least £109.45 (single) and £167.05 (couple), linked to earnings; residency‑based “citizen’s pension.”
- Replace Council Tax to benefit most pensioners; six months’ maternity pay at minimum‑wage rate.
- Tailored employment support replacing one‑size‑fits‑all schemes; end harsh sanctions on genuine claimants.
- Replace the Child Support Agency with HMRC‑based assessment/enforcement plus specialist tribunal.
- £200 Winter Fuel Payment extended to severely disabled working‑age people; option to invest a year’s payment in insulation.
- Strengthen protection for failed occupational pensions; consult and honour accrued public‑sector pension rights.
- Reduce fraud/error through simplification and prevention.

Housing, local services and environment
- Release public land for 100,000 affordable homes; encourage brownfield reuse via VAT reform; require permission for second homes in pressured areas.
- Restore Lottery independence; increase core arts funding with inflation; support grassroots sport.
- Devolve more powers; streamline inspectorates; protect post offices and universal postal service.
- Zero‑waste goal; 60% household recycling within seven years; producer responsibility; climate‑aware planning/building rules.

Transport
- Rail reform with fewer, longer franchises; shift road funds to station safety and key upgrades.
- Reform Vehicle Excise Duty to zero for least‑polluting cars; expand congestion charging tied to upfront public transport investment; long‑term national road pricing to replace fuel duty and VED.
- Free off‑peak local bus travel for pensioners/disabled; free railcards for pensioners, disabled people, families and youth.
- Limit major new roads; grow rail freight; develop ports/waterways; aviation: per‑aircraft charging, emissions trading, oppose new SE expansions.

Rural, agriculture and fisheries
- Fair‑trading duty and Food Trade Inspector to protect farm gate prices.
- Accelerate CAP reform toward public goods; support family farms and new entrants.
- Marine Act with conservation zones and regional co‑management; stronger wildlife protection.
- Animal Protection Commission and comprehensive Animal Welfare Act.
- Precaution on GM crops, support GM‑free zones, rigorous labelling; promote organic.

Europe, international affairs and defence
- Support EU institutional reform subject to referendum; prepare for euro entry if conditions met.
- Iraq: back democratic transition, build Iraqi capacity, and aim to withdraw forces with UN mandate expiry.
- Multilateral security, UN and EU reform, human rights focus.
- Defence: address overstretch; improve procurement; reprioritise programmes; maintain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament; tighter arms‑export oversight; back an international arms trade treaty.
- International development: increase aid to 0.5% GNI by 2007/08 and 0.7% by 2011; end agricultural dumping; fair trade access; responsible investment; green development priorities; stronger action on global environmental crime; lead on climate targets (Kyoto plus “contraction and convergence”).

Constitution and governance
- War Powers Act; Civil Service Act; stronger parliamentary scrutiny; reduce departments/ministers; decentralise to local/regional bodies; fair funding across the UK.
- Extend STV to local and national elections; predominantly elected second chamber; voting age aligned with other civic responsibilities; reform BBC governance via an independent regulator.
- Environmental Responsibility Act; green public procurement; merge key portfolios into a single environment/transport/energy department.

TEXT_C:
This 2005 manifesto proposes changes across the economy, environment, welfare, public services, transport, democracy, and international policy.

Economy and taxation
- More progressive income tax bands (illustrative: 50% over £50k; 60% over £100k) and additional corporation tax bands (up to 40% on profits over £1.5m).
- Shift taxation from labour and consumption to resource use and pollution: abolish National Insurance, phase out VAT, introduce revenue‑neutral eco‑taxes (including aviation fuel; levies on plastic bags).
- Pilot a Land Value Tax set locally to replace Council Tax and Uniform Business Rates.
- Promote economic localisation: community banks, credit unions, local currencies, support for small businesses; oppose joining the euro; seek reform of global trade rules.
- Job creation via renewable energy, low‑carbon transport, and zero‑waste industries; defend workplace rights and reduce working hours.
- Supplement GDP with well‑being metrics (e.g., ISEW/MDP).

Energy and climate
- Adopt Contraction and Convergence: cut CO2 by 20% (2010), 50% (2020), 85% (2030); develop full carbon trading.
- Replace domestic energy VAT and the Climate Change Levy with a Carbon Tax based on fuel carbon content; abolish standing charges; protect low‑use consumers.
- Reach 40% renewable energy by 2020; redirect nuclear subsidies to renewables; deploy solar, small‑scale wind, offshore wind/wave, and biogas.
- Warmer Homes Act to cut domestic energy demand 30% in 10 years; local “Smart Energy Councils” targeting 45% emissions cuts by 2020.
- Decommission nuclear plants at end of life; end nuclear R&D support.

Welfare, housing, work and families
- Phase in a universal, non‑means‑tested Citizen’s Income; retain specialist benefits and initially retain housing benefit.
- Introduce a universal Citizen’s Pension, earnings‑linked, replacing Pension Credit.
- Simplify child support and increase child benefit in the first phase; end the Working Time Directive opt‑out; explore a 35‑hour week; expand early‑years centres.
- Boost affordable housing: let councils reinvest sale receipts, support self‑build co‑ops, apply LVT, and upgrade insulation/efficiency.

Health and education
- Restore a universal NHS free at point of use; end PPPs and resist service liberalisation.
- Abolish prescription charges; reintroduce free eye tests and NHS dental care; expand access to complementary treatments.
- Increase health funding to about 9% of GNP; consider a hypothecated NHS tax; redirect future defence savings to health.
- Increase education funding (pre‑school and post‑16), scrap tuition fees, restore maintenance grants, abolish SATs, and promote individual learning plans.

Transport
- Target a 10% road‑traffic reduction by 2010; divert £30bn from road building to public transport; re‑regulate buses.
- Return rail and Tube to public ownership; expand lines, stations, freight, and light rail.
- Reflect full motoring costs via congestion charging/road pricing; raise fuel duty; abolish car tax discs; vary freight duty by size/axle/pollution; fund R&D in efficient vehicles.
- Restrain aviation growth: oppose new runways, ban night flights, seek EU aviation fuel tax; tax domestic flight emissions; raise Air Passenger Duty; shift short‑haul to rail.

Environment, food, and animal welfare
- Zero Waste Strategy: ban incineration, reduce packaging, set recycled content standards, create a Zero Waste Agency; aim for 60% domestic recycling by 2010.
- Environmental Protection Commission; eco‑taxes on aggregates, pesticides, organochlorines, fossil fuels; strengthen chemicals regulation.
- Apply the precautionary principle to GM, xenotransplantation, and nanotechnology; oppose patents on natural resources.
- Animal welfare: extend hunting bans, replace vivisection, end live exports, ban battery eggs (including enriched), tighten broiler rules, ban fur imports.
- Organics Target Bill: 30% organic production by 2012; support local food chains; ban GM food.
- Replace CAP/CFP with policies backing local markets, biodiversity, and sustainable incomes for farming and fishing.

Crime and justice
- Prevention through urban design, youth facilities, rapid repairs, more caretakers; treat drug use as a health issue; reject ID cards and redirect funds to prevention.
- Strengthen community policing, accountability, and local stations; revive community wardens/keepers.
- Tighten gun laws: quantitative lethality threshold, broader prohibitions, treat deactivated guns as active for licensing, single rigorous licensing, ongoing expert review.
- Expand restorative justice; enhance responses to hate crimes, violence against women; support stronger disability rights.

Democracy and constitutional reform
- Oppose national ID cards.
- Devolve power to local and regional levels; introduce proportional representation for local and national elections.
- Enable local recall (40%) and referenda (20% trigger); empower local taxation via LVT.
- Fully elected upper chamber by PR; draft a written constitution; disestablish the state church; limit monarchy’s formal roles.
- Oppose the proposed EU constitution while advocating EU reform to enhance democracy and sustainability.

International policy
- Ethical foreign policy: prioritise diplomacy, UN peacekeeping, and conflict prevention; withdraw troops from Iraq in favour of UN peacekeepers.
- Reduce defence spending to EU average; decommission nuclear weapons; end arms export subsidies/credits; negotiate an Arms Trade Treaty; ban use of depleted uranium.
- Raise aid to at least 1% of GNI by 2010; cancel debts of 52 poorest countries; support a Tobin tax; enable North–South carbon finance flows.
- Reform UN Security Council (end permanent seats; majority voting); democratise IMF/World Bank.
- Overhaul global trade rules to permit localisation and sustainability, replacing or modifying WTO with a General Agreement on Sustainable Trade.
- Asylum/migration: uphold refugee rights, speed decisions, allow work/benefits, provide independent appeals; ratify the UN Migrant Workers Convention; review domestic asylum law; support improved EU standards.

Judge whether TEXT_D or TEXT_C aligns more closely with this profile, taking into account that each foundation may be invoked in either direction.

Respond with a single JSON object and nothing else. Do not wrap it in markdown code fences and do not add commentary before or after it. The object must have exactly these keys, in this order:

{
  "evidence": "<the specific commitments in each text you relied on>",
  "reasoning": "<two sentences connecting that evidence to the verdict>",
  "confidence": "high" | "medium" | "low",
  "winner": "TEXT_D" | "TEXT_C"
}
